The archived city page of Barnaul is a general gas safety notice about trunk pipelines. It gives no length, size, date or owner for this pipeline.

A Bankfax item from the 1990s says the Novosibirsk-Barnaul gas pipeline, 292 kilometers, was finished by the end of 1996. Used for length and start year on P2283. It also lists planned lines from Barnaul to Biysk, Rubtsovsk and Slavgorod.
The page is the retired World LNG Dashboard and says it is no longer available. It says nothing about this pipeline.
A 2016 article about an 8.5 kilometer local gas line in the village of Pavlovsk. It is a distribution line, not the Barnaul-Shakhi trunk segment, and states no figure for this row.

A 2020 Politsib article says the Pavlovsk to Rebrikha line was started in 2016, dropped by the contractor in 2018, and restarted by Tomskgazstroy with 15 kilometers laid. It supports the construction start year 2016 on the Shakhi-Rebrikha row, which the sheet already cites to this page. No figure for the Novosibirsk-Barnaul or Barnaul-Shakhi rows.

A December 2021 Altayskaya Pravda article says the Rebrikha trunk line was completed, 77 kilometers, 1.2 million cubic meters a day, 2 billion rubles. This matches P3368 length, capacity, cost and start year, and is already cited by the sheet on all of them. Nothing on the other two rows.
The archived contractor page for the Rebrikha branch line and gas distribution station has a title only and no figures in the text.

An April 2021 Rossiyskaya Gazeta article says work on the Pavlovsk to Rebrikha section began in 2016, stopped in 2018 and restarted in July 2020. It gives no length, size or capacity for any of the three rows.

A 2020 Federalpress article about design work on two new branch lines near the Kazakhstan border. The live page returned an empty redirect through fetch.py, so the Wayback capture was read. It gives no figure for these three rows.

A December 2020 Gazprom news item about the 2021 to 2025 program for the Altai Territory says about 600 kilometers of branch lines to Rebrikha, Rubtsovsk and Slavgorod. No figure for these three rows. Read via a Wayback capture.

An August 2021 Altayskaya Pravda article says 27 kilometers of trunk line were laid from Pavlovsk toward Rebrikha, and the trunk line is 74 kilometers. This differs slightly from the 77 kilometers on the sheet, which comes from the December 2021 article. No figure for the other rows.
The gazprommap.ru Altai page is a gasification program page. It does not name the Novosibirsk-Barnaul pipeline or give any figure for these rows.
The decree list of trunk pipelines holds no entry for the Novosibirsk-Barnaul, Barnaul-Shakhi or Shakhi-Rebrikha lines. Its Pavlovsk hits are other places.

A February 2021 Bankfax article says Gazprom plans 600 kilometers of branch lines to Rebrikha, Rubtsovsk and Slavgorod, and that the Rebrikha station should finish by the end of 2021. No figure for these rows.

summary: confirmed (caveat), no concerns; length and start ref added from Bankfax
